AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #19
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures 14 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Cleaning Waste Dispos? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures 14 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Cleaning Waste Dispos.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures 14 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Cleaning Waste Dispos.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures 14 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Cleaning Waste Dispos.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures 14 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Cleaning Waste Dispos.

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Disinfecting Clothing and Household Articles 12 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Gr? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Disinfecting Clothing and Household Articles 12 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Gr.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Disinfecting Clothing and Household Articles 12 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Gr.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Disinfecting Clothing and Household Articles 12 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Gr.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Disinfecting Clothing and Household Articles 12 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Gr.

3. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

4. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

5. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Primary consumers only

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Conserving Animal Feed: Hay? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Conserving Animal Feed: Hay.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conserving Animal Feed: Hay.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Conserving Animal Feed: Hay.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Conserving Animal Feed: Hay.

7. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only water vapour

8. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Water always increases oxygen

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Organic Gardening 14 2.2 Storage of Crop Produce 10 2.3 Cooking: Using Flour Mix? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Organic Gardening 14 2.2 Storage of Crop Produce 10 2.3 Cooking: Using Flour Mix.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Organic Gardening 14 2.2 Storage of Crop Produce 10 2.3 Cooking: Using Flour Mix.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Organic Gardening 14 2.2 Storage of Crop Produce 10 2.3 Cooking: Using Flour Mix.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Organic Gardening 14 2.2 Storage of Crop Produce 10 2.3 Cooking: Using Flour Mix.

10. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Conserving Leftover Food? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Conserving Leftover Food.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Conserving Leftover Food.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Conserving Leftover Food.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conserving Leftover Food.

12. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. watt (W)
   C. joule (J)
   D. pascal (Pa)

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Homemade Sun Dryer and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Conserving Animal Feed: Hay and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Conserving Leftover Food and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Integrated Farming and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking: Using Flour Mixtures 14 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Cleaning Waste Dispos.

2. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Disinfecting Clothing and Household Articles 12 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Gr.

3. A — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

4. B — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

5. A — Producers

6. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conserving Animal Feed: Hay.

7. C — Glucose and oxygen

8. B — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

9. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Organic Gardening 14 2.2 Storage of Crop Produce 10 2.3 Cooking: Using Flour Mix.

10. C — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

11. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conserving Leftover Food.

12. A — newton (N)

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Conserving Leftover Food; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
